MacPaw announces a long-term strategic partnership with Liquid AI to jointly develop an on-device AI technology suite designed specifically for Mac.

The partnership will first start with Eney, the macOS AI assistant under MacPaw.

MacPaw and Liquid AI join forces to bring more on-device AI to Mac

Liquid AI's Liquid Foundation Models (LFMs) will be tailored for Mac assistant applications, and integrated with MacPaw's proprietary on-device technologies: the memory module Mnemos and the inference module Elix.

Eney switched to local models last year, keeping inference, contextual search, skill execution and conversation history on-device whenever possible.

This new partnership aims to further advance this direction. The two companies will jointly develop the underlying technology architecture, rather than MacPaw simply integrating another third-party model.

MacPaw says that once the new technology is tested and deployed in Eney, it plans to extend it to more of its products, and also hopes to open up the jointly developed AI technology architecture to Mac developers through Setapp.

This will allow participating applications to expose more features and contextual information to Eney, enabling the assistant to understand the internal state of the applications, thereby providing more useful answers or performing relevant actions.

To learn more about MacPaw's on-device AI technology and today's announcement, please click here; you can also click here to learn about Liquid AI's latest developments.
